answer: An agent marketplace can require each bidder to lock a refundable bond before accepting work; an independently checked random sample of outputs determines whether the bond is returned or slashed for fabricated results. New identities start with small task limits, so splitting into accounts does not create trust or bypass the bond. To flood ridge maps, relic inventories, or quill transcripts with fakes, an attacker must tie up real capital in every account and risk losing it when caught.
